title: Persist partial gradients in save_state for mid-accumulation checkpoints
problem_type: 梯度累积窗口中段保存的 checkpoint 恢复 step 但不恢复 param.grad（不属于任何 state dict），续跑的梯度求和不完整，最终权重与不中断运行差 4 个数量级
approach: save_state 按模型捕获 {参数名: 梯度}，save_accelerator_state 写 gradients_{i}.bin（仅窗口中段有内容，边界 checkpoint 无文件即向后兼容），load_accelerator_state 按参数名恢复

items.author: Michael-RDev
items.summary: DDP reloads the main rank's partial gradients on every rank (2-process CPU test diverges); stale gradients.bin survives an overwrite save with no gradients; a hook that removes a model shifts the gradient file indices so the next model loads the wrong gradients

claims.text: the full `test_state_checkpointing.py` file is 22 passed / 2 skipped (GPU-only). ruff check/format clean on all touched files.

limitations: Not verified locally: the exact divergence numbers of the reviewer's two-process script (my symmetric-data two-rank harness keeps local gradients identical across ranks, so both schemes coincide there); the per-process files address the mechanism structurally, and CI runs the full matrix remotely.

`ruff check`: finding counts on the touched files unchanged vs `main` for `accelerator.py` (22 → 22) and reduced for `checkpointing.py` (8 → 6, the restructured save block drops two pre-existing hits); `ruff format --check` clean.

limitations: Verified CPU/single-process (matching the issue's environment); multi-rank DDP writes gradients from the main process only (grads are identical across DDP ranks), and FSDP/DeepSpeed/Megatron keep using their own checkpoint engines. Deliberately **not** persisted: `gradient_state.sync_gradients` (derived from the restored step) and optimizer scalars — both already round-trip.
